title: どうも, やっぱり and やはり
summary: When history helps: どうも began as "in no way can I say", and やはり means returning to your original focus.

blocks.text: It is usually not worth studying word history, but a few words are only clear with it. どうも and やはり are two of them.
Old Japanese said どうも言えぬほど: "to the extent that I cannot say it in any way". Said of thanks or apology, it means "inexpressibly", then simply "very". The phrase shrank step by step.
Each step drops the end of the phrase.
As a thanks or an apology, どうも means "very".
Without ほど, どうも言えぬ means "I can't say why, but..." and gives the meaning "somehow".
On its own, どうも is an all-purpose word.
やはり / やっぱり: back to the original focus

The kanji (矢張り, a bow drawn tight) are a folk etymology, but they capture the feeling: after being distracted, you return to your original focus. In your own writing, write やはり in kana, not 矢張り. That covers "just as expected", "after all", "also" and "still".

blocks.jp: やっぱりこの店が一番おいしい。
blocks.en: This shop really is the best, after all.

blocks.jp: やっぱり田中さんが一番上手だった。
blocks.en: Just as I thought, Tanaka was the best.

blocks.text: やっぱり: a change of heart
The meaning you will hear most is the change of heart: you were pulled away from your first feeling, and now you come back to it. It means "after all".

blocks.en: I'm scared... I'll go after all!

items: どうも = in no way (can I say): very much, or somehow.
やはり = back to the original focus: as expected, after all.
やっぱり is the casual form of やはり, and the usual "after all" of a change of heart.

questions.instruction: What did どうも originally mean?
options: In no way can I say (it)
questions.note: どうも言えぬ.

questions.instruction: Which word is the formal form of やっぱり?
questions.note: やはり → やっぱり.

options: やっぱり雨が降ってきた。
やっと雨が降ってきた。
どうも雨が降ってきた。
questions.note: やっぱり = just as expected; やっと would mean finally.

questions.instruction: Which sentence says "Somehow my leg feels heavy"?
questions.note: どうも before a feeling: I can't say why.

questions.prompt: やっぱり、食べるのをやめた。
options: A change of heart: I stopped after all
questions.note: やっぱり can mark a return to an earlier feeling.
questions.en: After all, I decided not to eat it.

questions.prompt: どうも can be a greeting on its own.
questions.note: It stands in for a greeting.

questions.instruction: How should you write やはり in your own writing?
questions.note: 矢張り is a folk etymology; kana is normal.

questions.instruction: What is どうも言えぬほど?
options: To the extent I can't say
questions.note: ほど = extent.

questions.instruction: What does どうも mean here?
questions.note: Without ありがとう, どうも can mean somehow.

questions.prompt: テストは難しいと思ったが、＿＿難しかった。
questions.note: やっぱり: as expected, after all.
questions.en: I thought the test would be hard, and it was hard after all.

questions.note: どうも before thanks means very much.

questions.prompt: 考えたけど、＿＿行かないことにした。
questions.note: やっぱり: after all, back to my first idea.
questions.en: I thought about it, but I decided not to go after all.

questions.instruction: What does どうも mean here?
questions.prompt: どうも、お世話になりました。
questions.note: どうも alone works as a general thanks.
questions.en: Thanks for everything you did for me.

questions.note: どうも before a feeling: I can't say why.
やっぱり shows it turned out as expected.
questions.en: As I expected, he didn't come.

questions.prompt: As expected, the shop was closed.
questions.note: やっぱり opens the sentence.
questions.en: As expected, the shop was closed.

questions.note: やっぱり: after all, I changed my mind.
どうも: somehow, I can't say why.
It can also mean somehow, or serve as a greeting.

questions.instruction: Which sentence means "After all, I'll walk"?
questions.note: やっぱり marks going back to your first idea.

questions.instruction: Which one shows a change of heart?
options: さっきは行くと言ったけど、やっぱり行かない。
思った通り、やっぱり雨だった。
どうも体がだるくて行けない。
questions.note: A change of heart: back to the first feeling.

questions.prompt: I'm scared, but I'll do it after all.
questions.note: やっぱり: after all, a change of heart.
questions.en: I'm scared, but I'll do it after all.
